overview.headline: How pH measures water acidity and quality

keyPoints.point: Neutral water has pH 7 on a range from 0 to 14, with lower values acidic.
keyPoints.quote: The range goes from 0 to 14, with 7 being neutral.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that water with pH five is ten times more acidic than water with pH six.
keyPoints.quote: Water with a pH of five is ten times more acidic than water having a pH of six.

keyPoints.point: Water pH determines solubility and biological availability of nutrients and metals.
keyPoints.quote: The pH of water determines the solubility (amount that can be dissolved in the water)

keyPoints.point: Abandoned mine drainage can be very acidic and harm animals and plants downstream.
keyPoints.quote: water coming out of an abandoned coal mine can have a pH of 2, which is very acidic

keyTerms.gloss: Measure of how acidic or basic water is
keyTerms.quote: pH is a measure of how acidic/basic water is.

keyTerms.gloss: Property of water that indicates acidity at pH below neutral
keyTerms.quote: pHs of less than 7 indicate acidity, whereas a pH of greater than 7 indicates a base.

keyTerms.gloss: Water with pH greater than 7 that indicates basic character

keyTerms.gloss: Reported scale where each number shows tenfold change in acidity
